body.x: Automatic doors that open only when someone presses a button leave out the people who find buttons hard to reach or use, including wheelchair users, older adults and children.

The Promise, a Siheung-based R&D company led by CEO Yongmin Lee, built XERO1 so that stepping toward the door is the signal. At KES 2026, the company is showcasing XERO1, an IoT-based hands-free access system, and wants to explore collaboration with government and public institutions, schools, hospitals, construction companies and architecture and interior design firms.

The system detects the natural action of stepping on the floor as a user approaches a doorway and opens an automatic door without a button press. Its floor pad needs no battery and no separate power connection, and at 3 mm thick it can sit beneath or be embedded in finishes such as carpet, tile and tactile paving, so an existing space keeps its design and circulation. The company designed it for general users, wheelchair users, older adults, children and people with visual impairments, following touch-less, barrier-free and universal design principles.

According to the company, XERO1 has been installed and operated in commercial facilities, where its usability is being validated. It has completed KC electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) registration, and the floor pad has passed IP57 dust and water resistance testing, static load testing above 300 kg and 100,000-cycle repeated load testing. In 2026, The Promise received the Good-Technology Award in the Smart Access System category at the 12th Korea Good Company Awards, hosted by Money Today.

The company is preparing to expand overseas and says it must adapt XERO1 to each country's building environments, automatic door systems and electrical certification requirements. It plans to look at markets where demand for smart buildings, barrier-free environments and universal design is growing. Using data from the floor pad, it is also developing services including visitor statistics, space utilization analysis and detection of abnormal situations involving older adults.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
